p: Figures in this example are illustrative. A loan officer disburses a loan of $1,000.00. After the charge-off date has passed, a repayment of $100.00 is posted, which blocks a new charge-off because it is a non-reversed transaction after the charge-off date. Later the same day, a Merchant Issued Refund of $900.00 repays the remaining balance in full. Because the amount balance becomes zero, the charge-off transaction is reversed; the refund itself is treated as a reversed transaction and does not count toward the block check.

tr.td: Blocked: non-reversed transaction after charge-off date

p: A refund that clears the balance forces reversal of the charge-off, while an earlier non-reversed repayment still stops a new charge-off.

An administrator opens a progressive loan of $900.00 with interest recalculation enabled and an annual interest rate of 0.00%, then attempts to add an interest pause. The application forbids the pause for this combination, so the repayment schedule is not broken and installments continue to post as scheduled.
With a zero rate and interest recalculation on, the system blocks an interest pause so the repayment schedule stays correct.
